english: Sun, you look upon gods and men. You set, and it grew dark; you rose, and as light you arrived. Sun, climbing the sky, protect us.
uncertain: léwks-kʷe: noun 'light' (NOM) or AOR.2SG 'you shone'
stéygʰont: read as neuter participle agreeing with sóh₂wl̥ (could be PST.3PL 'they were climbing')
séngʷs / stéh₂s: AOR.2SG, sun addressed

english: Bright Sky, it is getting dark. The sun has set and the stars have taken their stand. Your stars gleam. Your moon gleams; protect us. May Dawn, your daughter, come again.
uncertain: léwke dyéw: VOC 'bright Sky' + impersonal h₁regʷesyéti
stesth₂ḗr: PRF.3PL 'stand, have taken position'

english: Father Sky, a guest has arrived; he is dear. We give him gifts, and he has sat down. Listen to us; protect the guest.
uncertain: sédt-kʷe: AOR.3SG 'and he sat down', guest as subject

english: Fire, you who burn, you who cook, you who heat the water - the waters have grown warm. We have eaten and are sated. Fire, warm us.
uncertain: h₁yód: neuter relative agreeing with péh₂wr̥, verbs in 2SG
wódr̥h₂ gʷʰrént: neuter plural subject with 3PL verb

english: Dawn, Night is your sister. Night has lain down, and you have risen; the moon has set, and men have woken. Shining, Dawn, you come. Dawn, give us light.
uncertain: stéh₂s: AOR.2SG 'you rose' addressed to Dawn
ǵʰlóh₁ontih₂: feminine participle 'shining'

english: Earth, our mother, you who carry (us): we sing your famous name. We are satisfied; hold us up.
uncertain: nos: GEN 'our mother' (could be ACC with bʰéresi 'who carries us')
gʷéHyomes: root 'sing'

english: Perkunos, great striker, hear our word. You who thunder, who slew the serpent, who freed the waters, you are famous. The serpent lay in the waters, and you struck it. Then the waters went forth to the sea. Now, Perkunos, rain on our fields.
uncertain: gʷʰóne: VOC 'striker' (vs 'slaughter')
gʷʰéns: PST.2SG of a present, read as 'slew'
nos: GEN 'our fields' or DAT 'for us'
wódr̥h₂ ... gʷh₂ént: neuter plural with 3PL verb

english: Bright Dawn, you drive swift horses. You who shine, you came forth, and there was light. Your two horses stood, and men rejoiced. Dawn, give us great fame.
uncertain: léwks-kʷe: noun 'light' or AOR.2SG 'you grew bright'
h₁éḱwoh₁ (DU) after h₁éḱwons (PL): number drift
sth₂tā́m: AOR.3DU 'stood' (vs IMP.3DU)

english: Mother Earth, we plough your field. You who create grain, who nourish the cattle - the grain has turned green, the cattle are sated. Nourish us.
uncertain: ǵʰelh₃wéh₂: 'green/yellow'

english: Great Sea, you are great. You who swallow the waters - the waters have come to you. Your fish swim. Sea, do not swallow us; protect us.
uncertain: h₁ludʰónt: AOR.3PL 'have come' (vs participle)
mē gʷr̥h₃és: prohibitive with injunctive PST.2SG
misfit: méǵh₂s: animate NOM.SG predicate for 2SG addressee móri, which is neuter (cf. vocative méǵh₂ in the same clause); expected neuter méǵh₂

english: Bright Dawn, daughter of Sky, you shine. You who drive the night away, you who light up the lands, you who lead the sun: you have come, and the stars have vanished. Dawn, come again and bring us the sun.
uncertain: dʰéǵʰomn̥s: ACC.PL of 'earth', read as 'the lands'
wédʰesi: 'lead' (vs 'bind, marry')

english: Now, gods, listen to us. You were born of Sky and Earth. You who watch over men, you who give good things: grow strong, go forth, and protect us.
uncertain: ḱléwsete etc.: -ete is PRS/PST/IMP.2PL; imperative chosen
Hwr̥dʰté / gʷh₂té: AOR.2PL or IMP.2PL; imperative chosen
diwés-kʷe ǵʰmés: ABL 'from Sky and Earth'

english: Bright wheel of the sun, you shine forth. You who go along the path, who bring warmth, who light up the two paths. When Dawn has arrived, you rise, and the stars vanish. Wheel, you indeed are great. Give us your splendor.
uncertain: skondéyesi: root 'shine' or 'leap up' (two entries)
stóygʰoh₁: ACC.DU 'two paths' or INS.SG 'along the path'

english: Gods, come to us. You came to our fathers and drank the libation, and you gave them good fame. Now come to us and sit down.
uncertain: gʷm̥té, ph₃té, dh₃té: AOR.2PL or IMP.2PL; past reading chosen for the fathers' part, imperative for the rest
ǵʰutóm: participle 'poured', i.e. the libation
h₁wésu ḱléwos: 'good fame'

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.
uncertain: owis: unlaryngealized spelling of h₂ówis 'sheep'
aǵrom: not in lexicon in this spelling; 'field, plain' (h₂éǵros)
ebʰuget: augmented past of 'flee' (bʰewg-); not in lexicon
ḱeḱluwōs: perfect participle 'having heard'

english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, you who redden: you lead out the cattle; you have come; a sparrow has woken, and the cattle have stood up. A man drives them forth. Dawn, safeguard them.
uncertain: h₁rudʰéh₁si: 'you are red / glow red'
spḗr: 'sparrow' (unexpected but grammatical)
bʰérgʰe: root 'safeguard'

english: Serpent, do not creep to us. Perkunos has struck you: die! Poison, dry up!
uncertain: gʷʰént: PST.3SG of a present stem, read as 'struck'
wíse: VOC of wisós 'poison'

english: Father Sky, you are the giver of good things. You who give light, who set the stars in the night, who hear our word well, who gave names to the gods: you are bright and famous. Now give us good things.
uncertain: dʰéh₁s: AOR.2SG 'you placed' (homonym of 'god')
h₁uséwōm: GEN.PL 'of goods'

english: Earth, a man has died; take care of him. His name is famous. May his fame be imperishable.
uncertain: stérge: root glossed 'protect'; 'cherish, care for'
h₁syéh₁t: OPT of 'be' (vs 'throw')

english: Gods, may it rain on our fields. May the grain grow, may the sheep be sated. May the earth not dry up, may the waters not vanish.
uncertain: deywṓs: VOC with impersonal OPT.3SG h₂ur̥syéh₁t 'may it rain' (as NOM.PL it would need a plural verb)
wódr̥h₂ ... n̥ḱyéh₁t: neuter plural with singular verb

english: The horses then said: 'Listen, sheep! We see this, and our heart is pained: man, the master, weaves the sheep's wool into a warm garment for himself, and the sheep have no wool.'
uncertain: tu: not in lexicon; particle 'then'
agʰnutór: not in lexicon; 'is pained, grieves'
dʰǵʰémō: 'man' (earthling), not in lexicon in this form
sē: reflexive 'for himself'
h₂áwyes: 'of the sheep' (GEN), non-standard spelling
gʷʰérmom: 'warm', not in lexicon in this form
wept: 'weaves/wove' (root webʰ-)
text uses a different orthography (a-vowels, unaccented forms)

english: Sun, your two swift horses carry you. When Dawn has arrived, the two stand ready, and you go along the path. You who light up the path - your path is bright. Give us warmth and light.
uncertain: sth₂éh₁yetām: PST/IMP.3DU; subject taken as the two horses
gʷéh₂s: AOR.2SG 'you went'
nos-kʷe: enclitic -kʷe joins the two objects gʷʰérmn̥ and léwkm̥

english: [O gods (deywóybʰos: 'to/from the gods')], a son has been born to us. May he live, may he grow, may he become strong. Protect him, and give him fame.
uncertain: stérgete: IMP.2PL (vs PRS.2PL)
deywóybʰos: an ablative 'from the gods' reading is possible but weak
misfit: deywóybʰos: DAT/ABL.PL in the address slot, while stérgete / duh₃té (2PL imperatives) address the gods; every other prayer opens with a vocative; expected VOC deywṓs

english: Perkunos, swift striker, hear. You thunder; you give water to the earth; you fill the fields with water. The earth was dry; you rained; it drank the water, and the grain grew. Perkunos, fill our fields with water.
uncertain: h₂wérs: AOR.2SG 'you rained' (or IMP)
péh₃t: 3SG, subject taken as the earth
nos: GEN 'our fields' or DAT 'for us'

english: Father Sky, we are going a long road. Now make our way straight. May we not grow tired; may Dawn lead us.
uncertain: nos: GEN 'our way' or DAT 'for us'

english: The horses said: 'Listen, sheep! It pains our heart to see this: man, the master, makes the sheep's wool into a warm garment for himself; and the sheep have no wool.'
uncertain: ewewkʷ: not in lexicon; augmented aorist 'said'
h₂gʰnutoy: not in lexicon; 'is pained'
widntbʰós: not in lexicon; DAT.PL participle 'to (us) seeing'
h₂ówyom: analyzer offers 'egg'; read as adjective 'ovine, of sheep'
kʷnewti: not in lexicon; 'makes'
sébʰoy: not in lexicon; reflexive 'for himself'
h₂wlnéh₂m / h₂wlh₂néh₂: variant spellings of 'wool'
text uses a different orthography

english: Heart, do not tremble; a god protects you. Night, lie down; [dawn] will come. Heart, grow strong.
uncertain: kʷsép: VOC 'Night' (or LOC 'in the night')
mē tréms: prohibitive with injunctive
misfit: h₂usbʰós: DAT/ABL.PL 'to/from the dawns' standing as the only possible subject of SBJV.3SG h₁ludʰḗti; expected NOM.SG h₂éwsōs 'Dawn will come'

english: Wolf, do not go at the sheep. Dog, protect the sheep; the dog is awake. And the wolf is afraid: Dyeus sees you.
uncertain: bʰéwdʰeti: PRS 'is awake' or SBJV 'shall wake'
dedórḱe: PRF.3SG 'has seen / sees'
